name: Burundi
summary: A white saltire dividing red and green triangles, with a white disc in the centre bearing three red six-pointed stars outlined in green. The stars stand for the motto 'Unity, Work, Progress' and for Burundi's three ethnic groups.
origin: At independence in 1962, Burundi was a kingdom, and its flag had a drum and a sorghum plant in the central disc. After the monarchy was abolished in 1966, the drum was removed, and on 28 March 1967 the three stars were introduced.

symbols.name: Three stars
symbols.description: Red six-pointed stars with green outlines in a triangle.
symbols.meaning: The national motto 'Unité, Travail, Progrès'; also the three ethnic groups: Hutu, Tutsi and Twa.

symbols.name: Saltire
symbols.description: A white diagonal cross from corner to corner.
symbols.meaning: Peace, linking the regions of the flag.

history.label: Kingdom of Burundi
history.note: Drum and sorghum in the disc.

facts: Its 3:5 ratio was adjusted from 2:3 in 1982.
Royal drums (ingoma) were a symbol of the Burundian monarchy.
Jamaica's flag also has a saltire dividing four triangles.
clues: A white saltire with red and green triangles, and three red stars in a central white disc.
Its stars stand for three words in a national motto.
A royal drum was removed from its centre after the monarchy fell.
